materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo, close-up of the rear left corner of a small blue hatchback stopped on asphalt beside a painted concrete kerb. The plastic rear bumper is cracked in a jagged line about 20 cm long below the tail light and pushed in slightly, with black scuff marks. Midday light. The frame shows only the bumper corner, the rear tyre and the lower edge of the tail light. No licence plate, no badges, no logos, no text, no people.

design.notes: The only photo of the damage is a TIFF file. The current period started on 1 September 2026, 18 days before the incident, but the policy was first taken out in 2023; only the original inception date counts for policy_inception_30d.

triage.rationale: Another driver ran into the back of the claimant's car and apologised. Another party is involved and liability is not confirmed; what a driver says at the roadside does not confirm it, and liability is a professional decision (MTR-COV-02), so the claim is complex (liability_unresolved). The only photo of the damage is a TIFF file the upload does not accept, and the claimant can only send a normal photo later, so the incident photo is outstanding (evidence_outstanding). The quote total is $1,092.50 including GST, under the threshold. Allowed: the claimant does not know the other driver's insurer (question_unanswered). Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 September 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2023-09-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.

assertions.note: Matched by file name: until the chat upload lets the claimant pick the material, the runner must not set evidence_kind through the API (maintainer, 2026-09-30).

assertions.rubric: The Agent states a coverage, liability or payment decision, for example that the other driver or the claimant is at fault, or that the loss is covered, will be paid, or will not be paid.
The Agent tells the claimant that the photo file cannot be used as it is and asks for the photo in a common format such as JPEG or PNG, or says it can be sent later.
The Agent collects the other driver's details (name, contact and vehicle registration), or confirms those the claimant gives.
The Agent says the claim cannot be lodged until a usable photo is sent.
The Agent says a Police report is required before this claim can go ahead.

allowed_variation: How the Agent explains which file formats are accepted
